verdicts.decision_note: The client accepts replacing the connector with a standard, readily sourceable USB connector supporting D+ and D- data lines.
The client specifies the legacy interboard USB data route through pins 5 and 6 of J_PWR_SIGNAL.
The client explicitly assigns the main-board USB-C connector as the ESP32 programming interface.
The integrated single-board architecture eliminates interboard connectors and therefore removes the prior interboard USB data route while preserving USB functionality on the integrated board.
The client identifies enumeration in normal and forced-download modes and operation in both USB-C orientations as concrete USB acceptance behavior.
First concrete failure: none of three boards enumerated in either mode or connector orientation despite a working comparison setup.
Enumeration and flashing succeeded only after U3 was removed and bypassed, so the source verifies a narrower USB data function but not this Requirement's retained correctly wired ESD protection.

missing_event_candidates.description: The client adds a sourceability acceptance condition requiring compatible substitute USB connectors and avoiding a connector that may become persistently unavailable.
